Title: Son dies in England, parents caught in Pune lockdown appeal to UK govt for last glimpse - India Today
### Download App. NewsIndiaSon dies in England, parents caught in Pune lockdown appeal to UK for last glimpse. # Son dies in England, parents caught in Pune lockdown appeal to UK govt for last glimpse. ## Siddharth's father Shankar Murkumbi has appealed to the UK government to immediately release the body for final rites as he "this is the least he deserves as his last wish and his mother deserves a last hug". Son dies in England, parents caught in Pune lockdown appeal to UK govt for last glimpse London,UPDATED: Apr 7, 2020 08:30 IST. Siddharth Murkumbi, 23, a marketing student at the University of Central Lancashire (UClan) in UK went missing on March 15. His parents in Pune are now caught in the coronavirus lockdown desperate to get back the body for a last glimpse of their son. Siddharth’s father Shankar Murkumbi has appealed to the UK government to immediately release the body for final rites as he this is the least he deserves as his last wish and his mother deserves a last hug. However, Siddharth’s parents have been unable to either get his mortal remains back for the last rites or travel to the UK to collect it themselves due to the ongoing travel ban due to coronavirus. Police suspect Siddharth had committed suicide. Shivam, Siddharth’s senior at same university had met him just two days before the incident and said he could never imagine that he is capable of contemplating suicide. We received information from the police that Siddharth’s body was found on the banks of River Ribbie and it was taken to the mortuary at Royal Preston Hospital where the coroner process is being completed, said Shankar. In the UK a coroner is a government official who conducts an inquest into the manner and cause of death. The coroner from Royal Preston Hospital has since written to Shankar asking him to confirm if he would like to attend the inquest. However, the family has since decided not to attend the coroner’s inquest and delay the process. Also Read | Premature to forecast coronavirus lockdown end, says ICMR chief scientist. Also Watch | Premature to forecast coronavirus lockdown end, says ICMR chief scientist. Apr 7, 2020 08:15 IST.

entity_ranked_evidence.snippet:
Title: Captain MV Pranjal's Parents Pay Last Respects To Martyred Soldier Son | Times Now
Captain MV Pranjal's Parents Walk Barefoot To Lay Wreath On Son's Coffin. ## The grieving parents of the martyred Army Officer were a picture of grace and self-control as they went through the steps of the military funeral protocol without betraying the hollow left inside their hearts due to the loss of their only son. Parents of Captain MV Pranjal Pay Last Respects to Martyred Son. Parents of Captain MV Pranjal Pay Last Respects to Martyred Son. **Bengaluru:** Just like one does inside a temple or bowing down before the idol inside the sanctum sanctorum, the grieving parents, wife, and relatives paid their last respects to martyred Captain MV Pranjal by walking up to his coffin barefoot. One can clearly see in the video where the grieving family arrives silently at the military funeral where the hero son of India lies in state at HAL Airport, Bengaluru. The parents walk behind the army personnel leading them and another one hands them the floral wreath. The parents (even the wife and relatives - later - when it is their turn) step out of their shoes, just as one dooes when paying respect to someone in an exalted position - and then walk silently to his coffin. The son of former Managing Director of Mangalore Refinery and Petrochemicals Ltd., (MRPL) MV Venkatesh and Anuradha Venkatesh, Captain Pranjal had his early education at the Delhi Public School on the MRPL campus in Mangaluru. In his final message to his wife, Aditi, Captain Pranjal conveyed his participation in an upcoming operation and assured a call or message on Thursday. As per the Army protocol, the Next Of Kin was contacted to convey that their bravehearted son had laid down his life for the safety of the nation. The family’s world was shattered when news of his death reached them on Wednesday, as four soldiers, including Captain Pranjal, were killed in the encounter. Captain Pranjal was due for promotion to the rank of Major on December 9. England is being sent back inside, a return to a national lockdown after a troublesome surge of **Covid-19** cases. Since the start of the pandemic in the UK there have been 1,011,660 cases and 46,555 deaths, a statistical death rate of 4.5%. The BritishPM Boris Johnson says the second wave of infections threatened to overwhelm the country’s health service. The UK which has ended up with the highest official death toll in Europe from Covid-19, is tying to cope with more than 20,000+ new cases a day. Health officials are warning of a “worst case scenario” of 80,000+ dead. The news of the new lockdown measures was leaked to the media so Mr. Johnson had to hastily convene a public press announcement. He says that the 1-month lockdown across England will start after midnight on Thursday and last until December 2. People will only be allowed to leave home for specific reasons such as education, hopping for essentials, work, exercise or caring for the vulnerable. The government is reviving its emergency coronavirus wage subsidy scheme to ensure workers who are temporarily laid off during a new England-wide lockdown receive 80% of their pay. • Pubs and restaurants will be shut apart from for takeaways. • Places of worship will remain open for private prayer, tfunerals will be limited to close family members only. The measures bring England into line with measures in France and Germany. Johnson was earlier criticised by political opponents for moving too slowly to initiate the first national lockdown, which ended up running from March 23 to July 4. The British PM eventually succumbed to a bout with Covid-19 in late March and was hospitalised in early April. This article is brought to you by our exclusive subscriber partnership with our sister title USA Today, and has been written by our American colleagues. AN East Lancashire teacher is bidding to inspire England's rugby stars by taking them to the Somme battlefield in Northern France. Paul Garlington, head of history at Stonyhurst St Mary's Hall, Hurst Green, came up with the idea to help the squad's World Cup preparations He said he discussed the idea with former England star and Stonyhurst pupil Will Greenwood. This led to England head coach Brian Ashton, head of rugby at Stonyhurst College between 1980 and 1987, asking him to arrange the visit. Mr Garlington, an expert on the First World War battlefields, said: "As the World Cup is in France this year, and considering that a number of England rugby internationals died on The Somme, I felt it appropriate that they should visit war graves to pay their respects. "For today's rugby stars to pay their respects in this way is a modern example of patriotism and the England squad should be complimented for it.". Mr Garlington, who also coaches rugby at the Catholic boarding and day school, added: "The intention is to add an extra dimension to their preparations and to boost their national pride.". Among them are four England rugby internationals. A total of 27 rugby players lost their lives during the Great War. Brian Ashton said: "On behalf of the whole squad we feel it is important to visit the grave sites to pay our respects to all the brave soldiers who lost their lives fighting for their country.". ## Get *involved* with the news. Italy is among some countries in Europe starting to ease lockdown restrictions. Italians strolled in the park, grabbed takeaway coffees and paid their respects to the astonishing number of dead as the first and longest lockdown in Europe was eased. Greece, Portugal and Belgium also wound back some virus restrictions on Monday, with Britain poised to soon overtake Italy as the country with the most confirmed COVID-19 dead in Europe. Traffic increased in city centres, commuter and long-distance trains sold out and more people ventured out after restrictions on movement eased for the first time since Italy locked down on March 11. Man with light brown hair and dark eyebrows and eyes wearing a black mask and blue gloves, holds a pole on a train. The Italian National Institute of Statistics (ISTAT), Italy's national statistics agency, reported on Monday that 49 per cent more people died in March than the average over the past five years, with 25,354 excess deaths registered from February 20 to March 31 at the height of Italy's outbreak.
